If AGENTS.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session (its first 64 KiB); your other files are there to read with the file tools. ## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read game 70 and the remaining instructions, then play at 20k. I’ll focus on contesting a larger share early while checking whole-chain liberties and eye space before each commitment.

Tools and analysis code may inspect the current board, count liberties and check legality; never build/use an engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search, or a program recommending/ranking moves.

Critical improvement: count DISTINCT liberties of ALL endangered friendly groups before each move. Joining groups does not guarantee safety. Check again after selecting a move, especially if it fills a friendly liberty. Game 1 lost six connected stones because the sole liberty J4 was overlooked. Use current-position-liberties.js as a counting aid, not as a move selector.

Before tenuki, identify opponent's immediate captures and cuts. Treat groups with one liberty as emergencies and two liberties as tactical concerns. Near the first line, assess escape routes before attaching: F8 in game 1 became trapped after F7/G8, and chasing along row 9 did not create an escape.

Do not describe groups as alive, connected safely, or enemy stones as dead without checking actual liberties and eye space. Distinguish observations from unverified strategic impressions.

Game 2 improvement: liberty counting alone is insufficient. Check actual eye space and an exit before enclosure. W34 D8 joined the upper group but left two liberties and no established eyes. Running F9/G9/H9 kept two liberties without escaping. Capturing C8 with C7 created only one eye; B45 J9 left 17 White stones with sole liberty C8, which White could not fill legally. An enemy stone in atari does not establish friendly life. Avoid filling interior space merely to connect.

Opening C3/G7/C7/G3 against E5/C5/E3/E7 took four footholds. G5 was initially SEPARATE with four liberties; G4 physically joined G3/G5 with seven. Early C2/D2/E2 developed the bottom before upper consolidation. D7 restricted C7 to three liberties; B6 then B7/B8 removed its western room. B7 did not secure the corner. Review BEFORE the B7 commitment and before postponing upper development during C2/D2/E2: the later capture depended on opponent errors, not a proven opening.

C8/D8/E8/F8/G8 joined the upper-left chain to G7, retaining top-row room. White G6 took the direct link to G5. H5 joined G5 rather than playing separate H6 with H5 as a cut point. H7/J8/H9 nonetheless restricted the upper-right. Review BEFORE G8/G6 and H5/H7; these safe connections still allowed substantial contractions. H8 joined the upper chain, C9 closed its left end.

At move37 E9 split the actual top strip: D9 became private, while F9/G9 remained separate. E9 was urgent BEFORE G9: filling G9 first would leave contiguous D9/E9/F9 and allow White E9 to take the required separator. After E9, White F9 would have sole G9 and could be captured through the main chain while D9 remained. Actual White B9 joined A9/B8, leaving all three sole A8.

A8 captured A9/B8/B9 but remained SEPARATE with {A9,B8}. White reentered B9 with the same two liberties. B8 physically joined A8 to the upper main, ataried B9 at A9; White A9 was suicide while the main retained its other liberties. A9 later captured B9 THROUGH main, making private B9 alongside D9.

A6 captured A7 SEPARATELY with {A5,A7}; White A5 left sole A7. A7 joined through existing A8/B7 to the upper chain and preserved eyes. This was a checked short connection after capture, not an attempt to make life by extending a lone edge group.

F2/F3 joined all lower stones physically. H4/B3 protected lower edges; White A3 challenged the lower-left. B2/A2 closed that boundary through main; J4 closed the right edge. D3 claimed a shared point. F9 filled the shared top point while retaining private B9/D9.

F9 left White G9/H9 sole J9. J9 captured two SEPARATELY with sole H9; White H9 captured that stone immediately (no ko). The purpose was concrete: capturing reopened G9, and Black G9 joined the upper main. White J9 then joined H9 to J8. Net Black gain was ONE area point, G9; no claimed forced kill or extra eye. Count newly reopened J9 for White H9 after the recapture. A one-liberty capturing stone is acceptable only with such a checked benefit; do not copy it as a general sacrifice.

Before move71 exact area was upper18+two=20, lower16+fourteen bottom empties=30, total50. White28+three=31, plus7=38; projected B+12.

E1 joined E2 and divided the broad bottom region. White D1 entered with sole C1; C1 captured THROUGH main and made private D1. White B1 then had sole A1; A1 captured THROUGH main and made private B1. Each capture retained the other region/eye.

These two empty points are diagonal, distinct private eyes shared with the living main. Do not fill them merely to merge J1.

F1 joined G1 to the lower main, making G2 private. White passed, then Black passed. The opponent's passes allowed the defensive sequence to proceed; this does not prove every earlier invasion answer forced a kill.

- D8/E8 development restored those four D/E points:50. Restoration announcement delayed until after G8.
- G6 withdrew one:49.
- H7/J8 entry withdrew H7/J7/J8/J9:45, announced together after J8.
- H9 withdrew one:44.
- A8 capture restored A8/A9/B8, while B9 remained enemy:47. Restoration announcement delayed.
- J5 entry withdrew J5/J6 and contested H6:44, announced after F2.
- F3 added own outside point:45; B3 added one:46.
- A9 captured B9, restoring B9:47.
- A6/A7 gained two outside points:49.
- A3 withdrew A1/A2:47; G9 withdrew one:46.
- A2 reclaimed A1/A2:48.
- D3 added one:49.
- J9/H9/G9 exchange reclaimed G9:50.

## Final verification and lessons for game72

Final Black43, White28, empty10. Upper18 stones+private B9/D9=20. Lower main24 plus separate J1 one plus five private empties {B1,D1,G2,H1,J2}=30. White28+private B5/D5/E6=31. Black50 - White31 - komi7 =12 exactly, no dead-stone assumptions.

Correct exact final counts and this tactical success do not establish 9d progress by themselves.
